newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan Q3 net, oper net both lower.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan Q3 net, oper net both lower.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc said net income of $276 million in the third quarter was 23 percent lower than the $360 million of the year-ago quarter.
Before an after-tax charge of $42 million ($71 million pre-tax) for a new technology alliance, third quarter net income was $318 million, down 12 percent from a year ago.
Third quarter net income was 37 percent below the $440 million reported for the second quarter of 1996.
Trading revenues rose to $510 million in the third quarter from $399 million a year ago, a gain of 28 percent, it said. Investment banking revenue rose to $233 million from $195 million.
On a per-share basis, third quarter earnings fell to $1.32 from $1.78 a year ago.
Before the $0.21 per share after-tax charge for the new technology alliance, per share earnings in the latest quarter were $1.53.
Operating earnings per share were below the consensus estimate among Wall Street analysts. According to the Institutional Brokers Estimate System, the mean estimate was $1.58 per share.
Revenues in the third quarter were $1.55 billion, flat with a year ago but below the $1.76 billion in the 1996 second quarter.

Net interest revenue declined to $425 million in the third quarter from $507 million a year ago. Net interest revenue is the aggregate of interest revenue and expense generated by asset and liability management, credit-related and trading activities.
"Other revenue" fell to $69 million in the third quarter from $145 million a year ago. Included were net equity investment securities gains of $56 million versus $91 million.

"Year-to-date performance is well ahead of last year, although third quarter results did not achieve the levels of the first two quarters," Chairman and Chief Executive Douglas Warner said in a statement.

"The mix of our revenues reflected sustained momentum in client-related business activities, with investment banking revenues up more than 50 percent as our market share continued to grow," he said. "Trading revenues for the first nine months nearly doubled, and investment management fees showed solid growth."
Raphael Soifer, analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman, said that while third quarter operating earnings were below the consensus estimate, "the underlying results weren't so bad."
He said investment banking revenues set a record. "Trading was down (from the levels of the first two quarters) but that was to be expected given the markets," he said.
The decline in net interest revenue reflected "roll-off" of positions that offered wider spreads, he said.

Noting J.P. Morgan shares were off 3/4 to 85-1/4 in morning trade, Soifer said he was telling clients the stock could be bought on weakness. His rating remains short-term "hold" and long-term "outperform."
